I. Intro​

​
🔖

​

For app release approval rules, administrators can set review-required permissions for developers to reduce the review cost and improve the review efficiency.​

This article provides references and suggestions to administrators regarding the type and level of app permissions and the approval rules recommended by the platform.​

II. Description ​

1. Types and levels of app permissions​

App permission is a control mechanism that uses the server API provided by Lark to access or modify data within the organization, such as obtaining the organizational structure, managing personnel onboarding and offboarding, updating docs, and sending messages.​

Lark has designed corresponding app permissions for each API, and different app permissions can access or manage different organization data.​

After the app is submitted for release, the organization administrator can review the app permissions. After approval, the app can call the server API or listen to the subscribed event list. For all available permissions within the organization, see [scope list](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uYTM5UjL2ETO14iNxkTN/scope-list).​

Administrators can determine whether to configure automatic approval for permissions that do not involve sensitive data based on the app permission type and level.​

1.1 Types of app permissions​

Based on the identity used when calling the API, app permissions can be divided into two types: ​

​
250px|700px|reset

![](https://p16-hera-overseas.larksuitecdn.com/tos-mya-i-lojyj5t9n9/f67f8babbdee42dfa0201913dbfbff82~tplv-lojyj5t9n9-image-v1:0:0.image)​​

- App identity permission: The API is called using the Tenant Access Token. The range of data resources that the API can manage is determined by the app's data permission range.​

- Note: If your business scenario does not need to perform actions on user data, and only needs to perform actions on the resources owned by the app itself (such as creating a base in the app's dedicated directory), Tenant Access Token is recommended. Calling the API this way does not require additional authorization.​

- User identity permission: The API is called using the User Access Token. The range of data resources that the API can manage is determined by the permission range of the user identity.​

​

| Permission type​ | Description​ | Scenario example​ |
|---|---|---|
| App identity permission (tenant_access_token)​ ​ | When calling an API or subscribing to events with "tenant_access_token", the app must have app identity permission.​ ​ | For example, if an app named "My bot" uses "tenant_access_token": ​ - When calling the API to [create a Base](https://open.larksuite.com/document/server-docs/docs/bitable-v1/app/create), the owner of the newly created Base is "My bot".​ - When subscribing to [Docs events](https://open.larksuite.com/document/server-docs/docs/drive-v1/event/subscribe), the app can only subscribe to changes in Docs owned or administered by "My bot". It cannot receive notifications for changes to other Docs. ​ |
| User identity permission (user_access_token)​ | When calling an API or subscribing to events with "user_access_token", the app must have user identity permission.​ | For example, if an app named "My bot" uses "user_access_token" for a user named "Lily":​ - When calling the API to [create a Base](https://open.larksuite.com/document/server-docs/docs/bitable-v1/app/create), the owner of the newly created Base is "Lily". ​ - When subscribing to [Docs events](https://open.larksuite.com/document/server-docs/docs/drive-v1/event/subscribe), the app can only subscribe to the changes in Docs owned or administered by "Lily". It cannot receive notifications for changes in other Docs.​ |

​

1.2 Levels of app permissions​

App permissions can be divided into two levels:​

- Non-sensitive permissions: The sensitivity of the data accessed by this permission is low, such as accessing app ID, app configuration, API name, and other data needed for the app to run. So no review is required, and it takes effect immediately after applying.​

- Advanced permissions: The sensitivity of the data accessed by this permission is high, such as accessing documents, Calendar events, Messenger messages, profile photos, geographical location, and other data involving content and personal information. The request must be sent for review, and it can only take effect after being approved by the app administrator. ​

2. Platform recommended review rules ​

Based on the type and level of app permissions, the platform recommends the following review rules. For specific information about the API, see [Scope list](https://open.larksuite.com/document/server-docs/getting-started/scope-list).​

​

| Permission type​ | App identity ​ | User identity ​ | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-sensitive permissions​ | These permissions do not involve sensitive organization information and can be configured for automatic approval.​ | | ​ |
| Advanced permissions​ | These permissions involve sensitive organization information and require reviews. ​ Note: Unless there is a significant reason, request for advanced permissions will not be approved. ​ | Among these permissions, the app acts on behalf of the user. The user needs to grant permission to the app before using the app. Therefore, except for specific sensitive permissions, most permissions can be configured for automatic approval.​ Note: Specific sensitive permissions, such as contacts and messages, need to be reviewed to enhance organization security. ​ | |

​

​
